description: Team of one, just interested in learning, doing, and wondering what this is all about!
summary: Orbital Health is an app that manages daily health monitoring and periodic testing all in one simple space. Astronauts already have a plethora of tasks they have to be aware of throughout the day, and adding the pressure of monitoring one's health can be unnecessarily overwhelming. With this app, users are alerted of important health tasks on a calming interface. They are brought to simple questionnaires that probe the surface of an astronaut's health. The results are compared to the astronaut's baseline metrics, since everyone has a different normal, and a more specialized questionnaire will be prompted if there is a noticeable shift. Once complete, an assessment of your health will be shown, and any necessary steps will be outlined in a simple list. Every aspect of health is considered and a wellness space is available in the app. Orbital Health is designed to take a significant load off of astronauts and facilitate swift communication between crew and flight surgeons should dire problems arise. Hopefully it can mitigate some of the stress surrounding health monitoring, and free up time for astronauts to focus on their research.
details: Orbital Health is a user-friendly app designed to monitor an astronaut's health. Essentially, you enter the data collected from your pre-flight examination into your pre-flight baseline. 72 hours into your mission, you enter data from another examination into your in-flight baseline. This ensures that advice and monitoring is specifically tailored to not only you, but your new normal after initial changes after takeoff. The app includes extensive medical knowledge and questionnaires, a feature that flags a flight surgeon if there is a severe issue, a wellness space, and access to link bio-monitors and wristwatches for easy data collection. The project is intended to simplify the duties of self-health monitoring for astronauts, reducing their stress and freeing up time. Extensive research using medical textbooks and NASA resources were used. Base44 aided in app creation, and the app was predominantly coded in javascript. This project goes beyond a simple check in app; it simplifies the check in process, but has a deeper layer of specific questioning for when things are off. It also offers much more than simple data collection, and allows easy connection between astronaut and flight surgeon. Not everyone has the same baseline health, which is why there is a place to specify that. The app is also specifically designed with some of the most common health problems faced in space like SANS and space sickness. Beyond that, most every aspect of Spaceflight health assessments are included and presented to the astronauts comprehensively. From in-flight periodic check ins to laboratory results, they are all there. It was also tempting to make a much more exciting or complicated app, but in this situation, occam's razor seemed to hold true. Hopefully this app can be of use!
